mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive months with UNRATE < 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly decline in real GDP (GDPC1) of more than 1% signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% signals a broad-based contraction in supply-side activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -0.5% AND HOUST < -0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST decline by more than 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures per capita (proxied by RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of below-average RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in CPIAUCSL below 1% for three consecutive months signals a deflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and discourages investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of CPIAUCSL < 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of more than 0.4 percentage points in both UNRATE and PAYEMS signals a rapid labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month +0.4pp AND PAYEMS > previous month +200k in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both UNRATE and PAYEMS increase by more than their respective thresholds in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between monthly HOUST and S&P 500 returns exists, such that months with HOUST growth above 1% are followed by positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST > 1% monthly and positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample test.
